subject: Recap: May 15 discovery — inference cost priorities & decision criteria
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi@finnode.ai>, Asha Iyer <asha@finnode.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: May 15 discovery — inference cost priorities & decision criteria

Hi Ravi / Asha —

Thanks for the time today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard, what success looks like, and the immediate next steps so we’re aligned before we scope the pilot.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Raw unit cost for text-generation across your customer-facing flows is the top constraint (token cost + peak GPU utilization).
- Unpredictable latency spikes during daily batch runs (spikes tied to large bursts from scheduled jobs).
- Existing stack is a mix: experiments on open LLMs hosted on single-node GPU instances + a small fraction of traffic to a managed vendor for apex models. Priority is reducing per-conversation cost without materially degrading quality.

Success criteria (what Finnode needs to evaluate pilot as a win)
1) >= 30% reduction in per-inference marginal cost for the highest-volume flow (customer prompts with ~230 token avg).
2) 99th percentile latency within 250ms for interactive flows during business hours.
3) No customer-facing degradation measured by your A/B prompt set (AUC loss < 2% on your scoring).
4) Clear ops runbook for failover to an alternative model/region for peak events.

Technical notes we captured
- Current models: mixture of Llama-2-13B (float16) and a heavily guarded hosted LLM for sensitive cases.
- You’ve experimented with batch windowing in the batch ingestion pipeline but haven’t tried persistent KV caching.
- Open to quantization if we can validate accuracy on your prompt set quickly; lower-openness on any solution that requires model weight changes for security/cert reasons (need a clear verification path).

Initial recommendations (what Redwood would like to propose for the pilot)
- Short technical spike (1 week) to profile your 3 top workloads: per-token distribution, seq len distribution, and burst patterns. This tells us batching strategy and caching opportunity.
- Pilot: 6-week pilot on dedicated capacity with automated prefix/KV caching and adaptive batching; quantify cost reductions and run your evaluation prompts.
- Pricing model for pilot: fixed monthly seat + usage uplift credit tied to measured token reductions (we’ll share two options).

Next steps (quick wins we agreed on)
- Redwood: share pilot scope doc + two pricing options by EOD Monday (attached).
- Finnode: send sample prompt set + a redacted traffic extract (1 day of logs) and confirm compliance constraints for quantization (who signs off).
- Schedule a 30-min technical spike kickoff with your infra lead; proposed: Tue May 18 10:00am PT.

Thanks again — I’ll attach the scope and a very rough cost sheet so you have numbers to review.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0149

Attachments: 20270515-pilot-scope.pdf, 20270515-cost-model-estimates.xlsx
From: Ravi Menon <ravi@finnode.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Iyer <asha@finnode.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: May 15 discovery — inference cost priorities & decision criteria

Jordan — thanks for the crisp recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 30% cost reduction target is for the high-volume customer support flow only (the one with ~230 tokens avg). For other flows we’re flexible, but the support flow funds any pilot.
- Latency target is negotiable during batch windows; the 250ms P99 is for interactive sessions only.
- On quantization: we are open to int8/4-bit approaches but we need auditability (proof that behavior didn’t regress on our fraud-detection heuristics). Any weight modifications must be reversible and auditable.

We’ll share:
- sanitized 24-hour traffic log (S3 link)
- annotated prompt set and scoring script (A/B test harness)

I can confirm Tue May 18 10:00am PT for the spike kickoff — I’ll invite our infra lead (Asha) and our ML lead (same thread).

Ravi
CTO, Finnode Labs
ravi@finnode.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi@finnode.ai>, Asha Iyer <asha@finnode.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: May 15 discovery — inference cost priorities & decision criteria

Appreciate the clarifications — that matches our notes. Attached you’ll find:
- 20270515-finnode-pilot-scope.pdf: short scope (spike goals, pilot boundaries, roles, estimated timeline).
- 20270515-cost-model-estimates.xlsx: two pricing structures (flat pilot fee + measured-savings split vs usage credits).

Couple of asks for the kickoff:
- Please confirm an S3 link to the redacted 24-hour logs and the prompt set by Mon EOD so the SE team can prep profiling scripts.
- Any legal/compliance guardrails we should encode up front for quantization tests (e.g., require KMS logs, no model export off your VPC)? If so, flag that in reply.

Proposed agenda for Tue spike kickoff (30m):
1) Introductions + success criteria (5m)
2) Data and sample handoff review (5m)
3) Profiling plan: what we’ll collect and expected outputs (10m)
4) Next steps for pilot scoping and timeline (10m)

If that looks good I’ll send a calendar invite.

—Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi@finnode.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: May 15 discovery — inference cost priorities & decision criteria

Quick technical note from the SE side before kickoff — hi team, Marissa here.

A few things I’ll aim to validate during the spike and pilot:
- Token distribution and sequence length variance (to recommend batching windows).
- Prefix/KV cache hit-rate sensitivity for your top-5 templates. Even a small persistent-kv cache can cut compute by ~15-25% on stable prefixes.
- Quantization smoke test: we’ll run int8 and 4-bit quantized inference locally against your redacted prompt set and fraud-detection checks. We’ll produce a diff report (examples + aggregate metrics) so you get reproducible evidence.

On compliance: based on Jordan’s note — we won’t request model weights. All profiling can be done on request inside your VPC or against a snapshot you provide. For auditability, we’ll:
- produce a signed results bundle and test log (SHA256)
- run the quantization comparisons under your supplied scoring harness so you see exact delta on fraud heuristics

I’ve attached a very small checklist that the infra team can pre-fill before Tue: expected S3 paths, short-lived IAM roles we’ll use (read-only), and required contact for security signoff.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: rdw-se-kickoff-checklist.pdf
